checklist.fact: The City of Colfax, California (a small city in Placer County with a population just under 2,000) is issuing the RFP.

The City is procuring acquisition and implementation of a cloud-based accounting and financial reporting software system, including initial implementation and ongoing services for all applications provided by the selected vendor.

The City currently uses Fund Balance fund accounting software from Tyler Technologies (modules: Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing, Business Licensing), with five users.

Key objectives include a streamlined package capturing financial transactions with budgeting and forecasting, effective reporting and data analysis, auditable records, and dedicated technical support during implementation and annual contract renewals.
Proposals are due Thursday, August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST, by email plus an original hard copy, and late proposals will not be considered.
The RFP was issued July 1, 2025; written questions are due July 31, 2025, answers posted August 14, finalists notified September 11, interviews September 25, and contract award October 22, 2025.
The City's goal is to complete implementation and go live on July 1, 2026, in coordination with the new fiscal year.

Scope of work has four tasks: project management plan, software installation and implementation (including importing the prior 5 years of data), staff training with support for the first 12 months post-implementation, and ongoing technical assistance and support (including 1099 and W-2 e-filing).
Proposals are evaluated 45% on response to project goals and scope, 25% on technical support, 20% on fee proposal and implementation schedule, and 10% on information, qualifications and references.
The RFP states no budget or price ceiling, but reimbursable expenses cannot be unlimited and must be capped in the price proposal.
Respondents must provide documentation of measures protecting financial data and secure access controls (Attachment G), and disclose any use of workers outside the United States (Attachment C).

Attachment F (Software Abilities and Requirements spreadsheet) is a separate Excel document provided by the City and not included in this PDF; the City's standard contract is available only upon request.

specificity.reason: Components name concrete deliverables, phases, roles, methods (four-step migration, parallel close, runbook, ticket tiers) and dates; only a few areas stay generic.

feasibility.reason: Plausible, but the migration of five years of Tyler data, six modules including payroll and utility billing, and a start in late October 2025 leave a tight schedule. Sizing the team for one vacancy is unsupported.

consistency.reason: Respects the price cap, dates, offshoring, insurance and security constraints. Strain: 30-day notice alongside the 15-day notice, and the contract terms are not yet seen.

component_records.title: Discovery, account structure and implementation planning
component_records.description: Phase 1 mobilises within two weeks of award and produces the project management plan required by Task 1: a dedicated project manager and named technical staff, a personnel management plan, a work breakdown, a milestone schedule anchored on the July 1, 2026 go-live, and a risk register. Weekly progress, budget and timeline meetings are calendared from week one and minuted, with a standing agenda covering percent complete, burn against the fixed price, schedule variance and decisions needed from the City. The team reviews the City's auditing and reporting requirements with the City's auditor-facing staff and documents them as a requirements baseline, then recommends an account structure — fund, department, object and project segments with defined lengths and naming conventions — that supports auditable reporting and roll-up to the City's budget documents. The same phase documents the City's account number customisation abilities, showing how segments can be added, renamed, masked or re-sequenced by the City after go-live without vendor change orders. Deliverables: project charter, personnel management plan, requirements baseline, recommended chart of accounts, and a written account-customisation specification.

component_records.title: Cloud accounting and financial reporting platform (configure and host)
component_records.description: The core system is delivered as a hosted, multi-tenant cloud subscription configured to the City's chart of accounts, with no City-side server or database to maintain. It covers the full module set the City uses today: Accounts Payable with 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions and purchase orders with approval routing; Accounts Receivable; General Ledger; Payroll; Utility Billing; and Business Licensing, so the replacement is module-for-module rather than partial. Transaction capture is systematic and efficient — approval workflows, validation rules, recurring entries and bank/utility interfaces — and the budgeting and forecasting module supports multi-year projections, what-if scenarios and budget-to-actual monitoring. Reporting and analysis are delivered through a standard report library plus an ad hoc analysis layer with drill-down from any report line to source transaction, so staff can answer questions without IT involvement. Every transaction carries a full audit trail (user, timestamp, before/after values) with retained documentation attachments and period-close controls, so records remain auditable for future reference and for the City's auditors. Configuration is documented in a written configuration specification that the City signs off before testing.

component_records.title: Data migration of five years of history
component_records.description: The team extracts, maps, cleans and loads the prior five years of financial data from the City's current system so that historical balances, vendor and customer records, open purchase orders, utility accounts and payroll history are available in the new system from day one. Migration follows a repeatable four-step method: source profiling and field mapping against the new chart of accounts, two trial loads into a test environment with reconciliation reports, City sign-off on reconciled control totals, and a final cut-over load during the go-live weekend. Reconciliation is evidenced by trial-balance comparison at each fiscal year end and at the conversion date, so the City's auditors can trace opening balances to prior audited statements. Migration work is sequenced with Accounting and IT so that extract windows fall outside close and payroll cycles, and the cut-over plan includes a documented rollback point to keep downtime and operational impact to a minimum.

component_records.title: Financial report writing and parallel testing
component_records.description: A report-writing specialist works alongside City Accounting staff to build the City's financial statements and management reports in the new system: fund financial statements, budget-to-actual reports, a schedule of expenditures of federal awards support report, utility billing and business licensing operational reports, and the recurring reports the City's council and auditor expect. Each report is built, reviewed with the City, and signed off against a prior-year output so that the City can confirm the numbers agree before go-live. Parallel running covers at least one full monthly close in both systems, with a variance review that must clear before cut-over. This component also delivers the collaboration model with Accounting and IT — a single point of contact, a shared issue log, and agreed escalation paths — so that report sign-off and testing do not depend on the City's one vacant position being filled.

component_records.title: Training, manuals and go-live cut-over
component_records.description: Training is tiered to the City's licence levels and roles. Power users in Accounting and IT receive personalised, role-based training in the configured system, delivered in person or virtually, plus a written power-user manual covering configuration, period close, report building and user administration. All staff receive at least one recorded training session they can replay on demand, plus a staff manual covering their day-to-day tasks, so training survives staff turnover and the vacant position being filled later. Cut-over is executed to a written runbook over the weekend before July 1, 2026, with a go/no-go checkpoint, a hypercare week of on-site or dedicated remote coverage, and daily check-ins through the first close. Completion of implementation by July 1, 2026 is a contractual milestone in our schedule, with the critical path shown from award through configuration, migration, parallel testing and training.

component_records.title: Ongoing support, updates and annual e-filing
component_records.description: From go-live the City receives twelve months of post-implementation support included in the base price, staffed by the same implementation team so knowledge carries over. Support is delivered through a help desk and ticketing system with logged tickets, priority tiers, published response and resolution targets, and a monthly service report showing volumes and performance against those targets. Automated update and software-change communications notify named City contacts of releases, what changed, required actions and maintenance windows, with release notes and regression testing before each update is applied to the City's environment. The team supports annual e-filing of 1099s and W-2s each filing season, including form generation, validation and submission support, and remains available for continued support of improvements and daily operations through an assigned account manager and quarterly service reviews.

component_records.title: Delivery team, qualifications and references
component_records.description: The bid names the project manager, implementation lead, report-writing specialist, migration engineer, security lead and training lead, with the office location of each and the hours during which the project manager is available for technical assistance. Our qualifications rest on a documented record of implementing accounting and financial software for local governments and other grant-funded public organisations, of advising clients on streamlining procedures to improve efficiency, and of providing continued support for improvements and daily operations; each is evidenced by project descriptions with location, scope, key staff and measured results. Three references for similar services are supplied with client name, scope, performance dates, contact name, phone and valid e-mail address, and we offer a local referral available for an in-person demonstration. The proposal also outlines virtual demonstration availability so the City can view product capabilities before award.

component_records.title: Price proposal and reimbursable expense cap
component_records.description: The price proposal is submitted on the City's Attachment A cover sheet and states a single total price for all services and deliverables, which is the total cost to the City including all materials, supplies and travel. It breaks out the implementation fee and recurring fees in detail, itemises licence fees by module and licence level, and lists additional support fees with implementation-period costs shown separately from post-implementation costs. It also estimates costs and fees for any additional applications or third-party vendors used to meet requirements, and states a fixed total reimbursable expenses cap with the reimbursable categories enumerated, so the City is never exposed to unlimited reimbursable expenses. The total price proposal amount is presented as the sum of the services total plus the capped reimbursable allowance, and the relationship between the three figures is stated explicitly so the City can evaluate on a single comparable number. All costs of preparing and submitting the proposal and of participating in interviews are borne by us and are not included in the price.

component_records.title: Governance, contract compliance and certifications
component_records.description: A single governance workstream owns every contractual, insurance, certification and disclosure obligation so none is orphaned in a technical team. We accept that all terms of the RFP are enforceable as contract conditions under the General Contract Terms and Conditions, and that "shall", "must" and "requirements" create binding obligations on us. We maintain a communications protocol from submission to award under which no one on our team, including representatives, subcontractors and suppliers, contacts anyone about our or others' proposals or qualifications, and we accept that a breach disqualifies us unless the City deems it harmless and unintentional and in the City's best interest. Our price proposal is final at submission and will not be altered or modified during clarification. We provide proof of workers compensation and commercial general liability insurance for this work, and documentation of the measures protecting financial data and the secure access controls implemented, covering encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access, multi-factor authentication, logging and monitoring, backup and recovery, and our independent security attestations. We complete the Certification of Financial Condition signed by an authorised representative, and we notify the City within 30 days and the Contract Lead within 15 days of any occurrence or condition that materially alters the truth of any statement in that certification. We disclose on the location-of-workers form whether any work is performed outside the United States, listing locations and corporate structure where applicable, and we give the City written notice if we or our personnel relocate work outside the United States during the contract.

component_records.title: Bid management, schedule and interview availability
component_records.description: We run the bid itself as a controlled project: a compliance matrix mapped to every RFP requirement, a single author responsible for the Section 4.2 order, and a red-team review against the four weighted criteria before submission. Written questions are lodged by July 31, 2025, and any exception to the City's terms and conditions is raised through the question process rather than in the proposal. The proposal is delivered as one signed original hard copy plus one digital copy emailed to accounting@colfax-ca.gov by August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST with the required subject line, and the hard copy is couriered to arrive before the same deadline. The named project manager and implementation lead are held available for virtual finalist interviews on September 25, 2025 if the City requires them, and the implementation schedule is built to start soon after the October 22, 2025 award so that the July 1, 2026 go-live is achievable.

From the date of the Certification to the expiration of the Contract, the Respondent shall notify the City within thirty (30) days of any occurrence or condition that materially alters the truth of any statement made in the Certification.
The Respondent must notify the Contract Lead within 15 days of any material changes to the representations made in the certification.
The Respondent must give the City written notice if it, its employees, sub-contractors, or other personnel performing services under the contract relocate to locations outside the United States.
Respondents must submit written questions by July 31, 2025.
Finalists must be available for virtual finalists' interviews on September 25, 2025 if the City requires them.
The vendor must complete implementation by July 1, 2026, in time for the new fiscal year.

items.text: The City of Colfax, California — a Sierra Nevada foothills town of just under 2,000 people in Placer County at the junction of Interstate 80 and State Route 174 — is the issuing body and the sole beneficiary of this RFP.
The City runs on annual budgeted revenues of $6 million with 11 full-time employees (one position vacant) plus one part-time/seasonal/contract employee, and closes its fiscal year on June 30.

The City currently uses Tyler Technologies' Fund Balance fund accounting software with modules for Accounts Payable (including 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions, and purchase orders with approvals), Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing, and Business Licensing, and has five users.

The City is replacing its current system with a cloud-based accounting and financial reporting system that captures financial transactions systematically and efficiently, including budgeting and forecasting.

The business drivers stated in the RFP are the ability to generate reports and analyze data for informed decision-making, maintaining auditable records and documentation for future reference, and having dedicated technical support during implementation and through annual contract renewals.

The City's small staff and single-vacancy headcount mean the transition must be delivered with minimal disruption to a five-user finance function, so implementation support and training carry outsized weight relative to the City's size.

The City wants a single vendor to supply and implement a cloud-based accounting and financial reporting software system, including complete support for initial implementation and ongoing services for all applications provided.
The City's stated goal is to go live on July 1, 2026, to align with the start of the new fiscal year, with the project starting soon after contract award and negotiation.

Task 1 requires an approach and project management plan with weekly progress/budget/timeline meetings, a dedicated project manager and technical staff, understanding of the City's auditing and reporting requirements, and a recommended account structure for auditable reporting.

Task 2 requires software installation and implementation support including financial report writing, import of the prior five years of data, and collaboration with Accounting and IT to minimize downtime and operational disruption.
Task 3 requires personalized training and manuals for power users, at least one recorded training session plus a manual for all staff, and support for the first 12 months post-implementation.

Task 4 requires ongoing technical assistance: automated update and software-change communications, support for annual e-filing such as 1099s and W-2s, and a help desk or ticketing system for prioritizing support.
The City intends to award to a single respondent for all items, though it reserves the right to make separate awards, not award certain items, or cancel the RFP.

Proposals are scored on four weighted criteria: 45% response to project goals and scope, 25% technical support during implementation and ongoing, 20% fee proposal and implementation schedule, and 10% information, qualifications, and references.
Written questions are due July 31, 2025, with the City's responses posted on www.colfax-ca.gov by August 14, 2025.

Proposals are due August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST, with finalists notified September 11, 2025, virtual finalist interviews (if needed) on September 25, 2025, and selection and contract award on October 22, 2025.
Only qualified proposals are evaluated by the selection committee, and the City may reject any proposal on the basis of fit, form, and function as well as cost.
The City may select a finalist group to interview with City leadership or make a final selection without interviews, and price proposals cannot be altered or modified as part of clarification.
Respondents must submit at least three references for similar services with valid e-mail addresses, and failure to provide a valid email may result in rejection of the proposal.
The City prefers at least one local referral who is available for an in-person software demonstration, and Tab 1 requires an outline of virtual demo availability.

Reimbursable expenses cannot be unlimited: the price proposal must cap total reimbursable expenses and state a total price for all services and deliverables, with implementation fees, recurring fees, license fees, and post-implementation support broken out in detail.

Proposals must be one signed original hard copy plus one digital copy, no more than 20 pages, with up to 2 additional pages for the cover letter and 5 for appendices, organized in the Section 4.2 order.

The digital copy and all attachments must be emailed to accounting@colfax-ca.gov by August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST with the subject line "Accounting and Financial Software Submission", and the hard copy must reach Attn: Shanna Stahl at PO Box 702, Colfax, CA 95713 or 33 S. Main Street, Colfax, CA 95713; late or FAX submissions will not be accepted.
Respondents must complete and return Attachment F, the Software Abilities and Requirements Excel spreadsheet, which the City provides as a separate document not included in the RFP.

Attachment G requires documentation of measures protecting financial data and the secure access controls implemented, and Attachment E requires proof of workers compensation and commercial general liability insurance.

Attachment C requires the Respondent to state whether any work will be performed outside the United States and to list those locations and the corporate structure of any offshore personnel, which the City will weigh for risk and cost before award.

Attachment D requires a signed Certification of Financial Condition covering audit opinion, tax and lien status, and litigation, with notification to the Contract Lead within 15 days of any material change.

The City's standard contract with terms and conditions is referenced but not included in the RFP and is available only upon request; any exceptions must be raised as questions by July 31, 2025, since objections filed with the proposal will be disregarded or cause rejection.
The City closes its fiscal year on June 30, which is why the go-live milestone is set at July 1, 2026.
The City currently runs five users on Tyler Fund Balance, so discovery is scoped to a five-user finance function rather than a large department.

The City's current system is Tyler Technologies' Fund Balance with Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing and Business Licensing modules, which defines the replacement scope.
The City's current system holds the five years of history to be migrated, so extraction is from that source rather than from paper records.
The City has 11 full-time employees with one position vacant, so report building and testing must be structured to minimise demands on City staff time.
The City's stated goal is to go live on July 1, 2026 to align with the start of the new fiscal year.
The City's current Accounts Payable module includes 1099 filing and its Payroll module implies W-2 reporting, so annual e-filing support is a continuing need rather than a new one.
The City prefers at least one local referral available for an in-person software demonstration and requires an outline of virtual demo availability.
The City requires the price proposal to cap reimbursable expenses and to state a total price for all services and deliverables.
The City requires proof of workers compensation and commercial general liability insurance and documentation of financial-data protection measures as part of the submission.
The City's schedule sets written questions due July 31, 2025, proposals due August 28, 2025, virtual finalist interviews on September 25, 2025 and award on October 22, 2025.
The new system is assumed to be scoped for the City's current five named users with headroom to add users later, and all six listed modules are assumed to be in scope for replacement.

Support service levels are assumed to be defined by the bidder, so the proposal commits to published response and resolution targets and a monthly service report as the measurable standard for "dedicated technical support".

The July 1, 2026 go-live is treated as a firm contractual milestone, with the implementation schedule built backwards from it and a contract start assumed in late October 2025 following the October 22, 2025 award.

The Attachment F and Attachment G software requirements are assumed to match the functional scope described in Section 5, and the completed Attachment F spreadsheet will be returned with the submission once the City provides it.

The prior five years of data are assumed to be extractable from the City's current Tyler Fund Balance system in electronic form, with the City responsible for confirming completeness and the vendor responsible for mapping, loading and reconciling control totals.
The twelve months of post-implementation support is assumed to be included in the base price rather than priced as an option, and is assumed to begin at go-live.

The reimbursable expenses cap is assumed to be a fixed dollar not-to-exceed figure covering travel, third-party licences and other pass-through costs, and the total price proposal amount is assumed to be the services total plus that cap.

Insurance is assumed to be priced at commercial general liability and workers compensation limits customary for a California municipal software contract, with the City's specific limits and additional-insured requirements confirmed through the question process.
The Attachment G security documentation is assumed to be acceptable as a written narrative supported by independent attestations such as SOC 2, since the RFP does not prescribe a format.
Material-change notification is assumed to be given within 15 days to the Contract Lead, with the same notice copied to the City, reconciling the 15-day and 30-day deadlines in the RFP.

The City's standard contract and General Contract Terms and Conditions are assumed to be obtainable on request before the July 31, 2025 question deadline, and any exceptions will be raised as questions rather than in the proposal.
No work is assumed to be performed outside the United States, so the offshoring disclosure is answered "No" and the location-of-workers form lists only United States delivery locations.

Attachment F and G requirements not available before submission. The RFP requires the completed Attachment F software abilities spreadsheet and the Attachment G application requirements to be returned with the proposal, but neither document is in the RFP package. The proposed solution assumes both match the functional scope in Section 5 and that the spreadsheet will be returned once the City provides it. If the attachments list requirements beyond the six modules described, the fixed price and the July 1, 2026 schedule are both built on an incomplete scope. Two mandatory submission items (R100, R141) depend on documents the RFP does not include, and the solution's own assumption states the scope match is unverified. A missing mandatory attachment can make the proposal non-responsive on its own.

Fixed price and July 2026 go-live committed before the standard contract is seen. The City's standard contract and General Contract Terms and Conditions are only available on request and are not in the RFP, yet all RFP terms become binding contract conditions and exceptions must be raised as questions by July 31, 2025. The solution commits to a fixed total price and a contractual July 1, 2026 milestone before those terms are reviewed. Indemnity, insurance, termination or acceptance clauses discovered late could force either an unpriced risk or a withdrawal. R037 makes every RFP term enforceable and R026 rejects objections raised in the proposal, so the only window is the question period; the solution assumes the contract is obtainable on request, which the RFP does not guarantee.

July 1, 2026 go-live treated as firm on an eight-month schedule. The RFP states July 1, 2026 as a goal and leaves the contract start as 'soon after award', while the solution makes it a contractual milestone and builds the plan backwards from an assumed late-October 2025 start. Configuration, five-year migration, parallel close, report writing and training must all fit in roughly eight months for a five-user team with one vacancy. Any award delay, City staff unavailability during close or payroll cycles, or a failed parallel close pushes go-live past the fiscal year boundary. The RFP does not settle whether the date is binding or when the contract starts, and the solution converts a stated goal into a contractual commitment with no float described.

Five-year data migration quality and ownership undefined. The RFP does not state the format, volumes or quality of the five years of history, nor who cleans and validates it, and the solution assumes the data is electronically extractable from Tyler Fund Balance with the City confirming completeness. If the source data is incomplete, inconsistently coded or only partly extractable, migration and reconciliation expand well beyond the planned two trial loads and the cut-over weekend. The bidder absorbs the extra effort under a fixed price. R109 is mandatory and the reconciliation is tied to audited opening balances, but the RFP leaves source format and cleansing responsibility open, and the solution's assumption places completeness risk on the City without a stated remedy.

Support service levels and the 12-month support price are undefined. The RFP asks for 'dedicated technical support' without measurable service levels and does not say whether the first 12 months of post-implementation support is included in the base price or priced separately. The solution assumes bidder-defined targets and includes the twelve months in the base price. If the City expects tighter response and resolution times, or treats support as a separately evaluated line, the bid is either underpriced or scored poorly on the 25% support criterion. R113 is mandatory and support carries 25% of the evaluation weight, yet the RFP gives no acceptance criteria and the solution's service levels are its own inference.

Reimbursable expense cap set without a City ceiling. The RFP requires a capped reimbursable expense figure and a total price proposal amount but gives no cap level, no reimbursable categories and no rule for how the three amounts relate. The solution assumes a fixed not-to-exceed figure covering travel, third-party licences and pass-through costs, with the total equal to services plus the cap. If the City evaluates on a different basis or expects a lower cap, the bid is either uncompetitive or the cap is exhausted mid-project. R121, R123 and R124 are mandatory and the RFP leaves the cap basis and the relationship between the figures open, so the solution's pricing structure rests on an inference.

Insurance limits and security documentation format unknown at bid time. Proof of workers compensation and commercial general liability insurance and documentation of financial-data protection measures are mandatory submission items, but the RFP states no coverage limits, additional-insured requirements or accepted security format. The solution assumes customary California municipal limits and a written narrative backed by SOC 2. If the City's actual limits exceed current coverage or require a specific framework, the bidder faces a certificate it cannot produce by the deadline or an unplanned premium. R139 and R141 are mandatory and the RFP leaves limits and format open, so the solution's assumption is the only basis for pricing and for the submission package.

Conflicting material-change notification deadlines. The RFP requires notice to the City within 30 days of a material change to the financial certification and notice to the Contract Lead within 15 days of the same change. The solution reconciles this by notifying within 15 days and copying the City. If the City reads the two clauses as separate obligations with separate recipients and evidence, a single notice may not satisfy both and a missed deadline becomes a contract breach. R098 and R138 set different deadlines for the same event and the RFP does not say which governs; the solution's reconciliation is an assumption, not a City position.

User count and module scope not fixed by the RFP. The RFP lists the current modules and states five current users but does not say whether the new system must support only five users or more, nor whether every listed module is in scope. The solution scopes for five named users with headroom and all six modules. If the City expects a larger user base or additional modules, licence fees and configuration effort rise against a fixed price. R008 is mandatory and the licence breakout under R090 depends on user counts, but the RFP leaves both the user count and the module list open.

Third-party applications and vendors unpriced and unapproved. The RFP requires the proposal to identify where and when other vendors or applications will be used and to estimate their costs, but does not say whether third-party components are permitted or limited. The solution describes a single-vendor stack without naming third-party dependencies such as bank or utility interfaces. If any interface requires a third-party product or the City restricts subcontracting, the price and the integration design change after award. R062 and R092 are mandatory and the RFP leaves third-party limits open, while the solution's single-vendor framing does not address the interfaces it relies on.

City staff capacity during implementation. The City has 11 full-time employees with one position vacant, and the plan depends on City Accounting and IT staff for requirements sign-off, two trial load reconciliations, report review, a parallel monthly close and training. The solution mitigates this with a single point of contact and a shared issue log but does not secure named City time. If the vacant position stays unfilled or close cycles absorb staff, sign-offs slip and the go-live milestone moves. R110 and R111 require collaboration with Accounting and IT and the RFP states the vacancy, but the solution's mitigation is procedural rather than a committed City resource.

Proposal compliance and delivery mechanics. The proposal must be one signed hard copy received at the Colfax address plus a digital copy emailed by 4:00 PM PST on August 28, 2025, within a 20-page limit, in the Section 4.2 order, with Attachment F, the price cover sheet and the certification all completed. The RFP leaves the hard-copy deadline, the page limit and the required section contents ambiguous. A missing signature, a late courier delivery or an omitted attachment makes the proposal non-responsive regardless of quality. Several mandatory submission requirements (R040, R044, R046, R055, R056) carry rejection consequences and the RFP does not settle whether the same deadline governs physical delivery or whether the page limit is binding.
